messages:
Aisha: FYI I'm onboarding hf/asteria-base into staging. Did a quick int4 quant with our qconv flow and ran the en/ko + ja/ja retrieval tests — seeing a reproducible BLEU drop on ko->en polite forms and some weird RTL punctuation flips on ar->en. Anyone seen this pattern after quant? :eyes:
Li: Can you paste a minimal repro command? I'll kick off a controlled run.
Aisha: Sure — ran:
```bash
./tools/eval_translate.py --model hf/asteria-base --quant int4 --tasks asia_translation --out /tmp/asteria-int4.json
```
Sam: Reproduced locally on small sample. Example: source `\"고객님은 이 상품을 원하십니까?\"` -> baseline tokenization: `[0x8a, 0x2c, 0x9f, ...]` quantized run tokenization: `[0x8a, 0x2c, 0x9f, 0x4f, 0x1a]` (suffix split). Model seems to drop the honorific suffix and reduces politeness in generation. Small diff but it kills BLEU on polite-dev.
María: Also seeing embedding-retrieval degradation on ja synonyms. Top-1 recall down ~6% after int4. Looks like some embedding dimension collapse on specific kanji clusters. Could be quant kernel selection or int4 scale bias.
Aisha: Noticed the Arabic RTL issue when punctuation moves — e.g. `\"...؟\"` becomes `\"?…\"` in output ordering (i.e., punctuation reflow). Might be detok/NFKC mismatch + tokenization boundary changes after quantization artifact.
Li: Two quick hypotheses: (1) tokenizer normalization changed (NFC vs NFKC) between hf/asteria tokenizer and our packaging step, which interacts with quantized KV caching; (2) int4 kernel path uses different subword merge heuristics.
Sam: Quick diff of tokenizer.json before/after packaging shows different special-case map for U+FEFF and ZWJ handling. I'll dump token->string for the problematic example.
Sam: ```
# token ids -> strings (packaged vs raw)
packaged: 1234 -> "시", 1235 -> "\\uC77D", 1236 -> "\\uC2DC"
raw:       1234 -> "시", 1235 -> "ㅂ니다", 1236 -> "\\uC2DC"
```
Aisha: Great. Plan proposal:
- Run eval harness on full asia_translation split for float16,int8,int4 (same seed, forced decode)
- Run tokenization diff tool across the corpus to count boundary mismatches (we have a script: tools/token_boundary_diff.py)
- Bisect quant kernels: serve int4 with `--executor=minimal` vs `--executor=fast` to see if kernel selection changes outcome
- Try `use_legacy_tokenizer=true` packaging flag to rule out packaging normalization.
Li: I can run the float16/int8/int4 sweep on staging tonight. Will also run token_boundary_diff and attach the sample IDs. I'll try packaging with `--tokenizer-normalization=NFKC` as a control.
María: For embeddings: add a recall test that uses kanji cluster queries (we already have evalsets/ja-retrieval-kanji). Please record cosine distribution histograms pre/post quant.
ops-bot: heads-up: staging GPU pool auto-scheduler will need a 4x slot reservation for the sweep (requested -- ETA 45m).
EvalBot: Summary: initial reproducer shows ko politeness BLEU drop (delta -4.2) and ja retrieval R@1 drop (-6.1) on int4. RTL punctuation flip observed on 12/500 ar samples.
Aisha: Thanks. If bisect shows kernel-specific, we should consider pinning int4 to the more conservative kernel for now and file a follow-up with runtime + quant team. @Li pls post results and we'll decide on rollback vs tokenizer patch. :white_check_mark:
Li: Will do — starting runs now. Posting artifacts to s3://redwood-evals/asteria/2205554321/ when done.
María: If anyone wants me to run extra ja synonym clusters, ping here.
Aisha: Awesome — appreciate it. :sparkles:
